correctness.rationale: For any Hilbert pullback quadratic form, averaging the two-sided norm inequalities over permutations keeps exactly the same constants; 120-degree rotational invariance forces scalar Euclidean norm. Every nonzero zero-sum real triple is a permuted rescaling of (1,r,-1-r) with 0<=r<=1. The derivative numerator is G_r(p-1), strictly convex in its real argument with zeros at 1 and 3. Its sign yields strict global monotonicity except p=2,4. Evaluation of the two endpoints gives the displayed exact distortion and both limiting endpoint cases. The integral quartic identity and 20,020 finite radial checks were rerun from the included script; no enumeration is used to establish an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The real 3-atom mean-zero subspace is a canonical nontrivial hyperplane in classical ell_p spaces, and Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is a structural intrinsic invariant. An exact result across every p, including both endpoint norms, identifies a second exceptional Hilbert exponent p=4 and a reversal of the extremizing two symmetry orbits at precisely two points. The proof isolates a strict convex exponential-polynomial mechanism. This is a complete natural one-parameter classification rather than a computation of an arbitrary isolated norm or trivial substitution.
